evals.prompt: can you pull the text off https://example.com and also off https://docs.crawl4ai.com/core/quickstart/ — save both as markdown files under out/ please, I want to grep them later
evals.expected_output: Two markdown files under out/, one per URL, each holding the page's content text. The example.com file contains the heading 'Example Domain'. Neither file contains site navigation chrome.
assertions: Two .md files exist under out/ (one per requested URL)
Each .md file is longer than 120 characters (a silent empty extraction yields 1)
The example.com output contains the string 'Example Domain'
All .md files under out/ are free of the string 'Brand Book' (site navigation chrome); fails if no files were produced

evals.prompt: grab me the front page entries (title + link) from https://news.ycombinator.com as JSON — need at least 20 of them, write it to out/items.json
evals.expected_output: out/items.json containing a JSON array of at least 20 objects, each with a non-empty title and an absolute url.
assertions: out/items.json parses as a JSON array
The array holds at least 20 elements
Every element of the array has non-empty 'title' and 'url' keys
Every 'url' value in the array starts with 'http'

evals.prompt: my crawl of https://example.com prints an empty string. it reports success=True and status_code=200 so the site is fine. the config is CrawlerRunConfig(cache_mode=CacheMode.BYPASS, css_selector='main'). what is wrong and what does the fixed call look like?
evals.expected_output: Diagnosis that css_selector='main' matches no element on the page, causing success=True with effectively empty Markdown. A corrected call that omits the selector (or targets an element that exists), verified to return the page content.
assertions: The explanation names css_selector (or 'selector') as the cause of the empty output
The corrected call is shown or executed and its output contains 'Example Domain'
The final code either drops css_selector or uses a selector that exists in the target page
